Add synchronous command execution next, then a small filesystem. Leave code interpretation, sessions, and PTY for later.

Both SDKs already do the same thing in their own getting-started examples: create a sandbox, run one command, read the output. Daytona’s TypeScript and Go guides call `process.executeCommand` / `Process.ExecuteCommand`. Modal’s JavaScript and Go guides call `exec` / `Exec` and then read stdout. The lifecycle API can start and stop a sandbox, but it still cannot do the operation those SDKs treat as the point of having one.

## Exec first

One call, then wait until the process exits:

- argv, not a shell string
- working directory, environment, and timeout
- exit code, stdout, and stderr

That is the overlap. Modal already takes an argv and returns separate stdout and stderr streams plus `wait()`. Daytona only has a shell string (`ExecuteCommand`) and puts output on `result` / `artifacts.stdout`. Map an argv onto Daytona by shell-quoting each argument into one `ExecuteCommand`. Pipes and globs stay out of this call; a caller who wants a shell passes that argv explicitly, for example `["bash", "-c", "..."]`, which both providers can run.

Keep the same timeout rules you already use. TypeScript milliseconds, Go `time.Duration`, omitted versus explicit zero preserved. Daytona’s command timeout is whole seconds (`0` means no server limit). Modal’s `timeoutMs` uses `0` the same way.

Leave these off the first slice. They are real in one SDK and a different product in the other:

- Daytona `codeRun`, code-interpreter contexts, charts, sessions, and PTY
- Modal stdin streaming, PTY, per-exec secrets, text-versus-binary mode, and the sandbox entry process’s own stdin/stdout

A `RunCode` helper would only fit Daytona. Modal’s JavaScript and Go SDKs have no interpreter; Python and Node are just programs in the image. After `Exec` exists, running code is `python` or `node` on that argv.

## Filesystem second

Exec and files compose: write a script, then run it. That is the portable version of “code execution.”

Both languages on both providers already have the same core. Ship only that:

| Operation | Modal | Daytona |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Read and write bytes or text | `readBytes` / `readText`, `writeBytes` / `writeText` | `DownloadFile`, `UploadFile` |
| Make a directory | `makeDirectory` | `CreateFolder` |
| List a directory | `listFiles` | `ListFiles` |
| Stat one path | `stat` | `GetFileInfo` |
| Remove a file or directory | `remove` | `DeleteFile` |

Require absolute paths. Modal rejects relative ones. Daytona resolves them against the sandbox working directory, which is an implicit default worth rejecting before the provider call.

Leave Daytona search, replace, permissions, move, and streaming, and Modal `watch` plus local `copyFromLocal` / `copyToLocal`, out of this slice. Read and write bytes already cover the portable copy.

## After those two

Streaming exec is the natural third step: stdin and live stdout. Modal returns a `ContainerProcess`. Daytona needs a session and log streaming, so it is a larger mapping than buffered `Exec`.

Git, LSP, computer use, volumes, filesystem snapshots, tunnels, and image-build helpers are each one provider’s surface. They fit the same capability pattern as pause versus terminate, but they are not the next shared API.

| Module | Daytona only | Modal only |

# Filesystem

`Filesystem` reads and writes files inside one sandbox. Lifecycle stays on the
handle. Both Daytona and Modal implement these methods.

| Call             | Result                                                         |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ReadFile`       | Bytes of one file                                              |
| `WriteFile`      | Replaces one file and creates missing parent directories       |
| `CopyFromLocal`  | Copies a file from the caller into the sandbox                |
| `CopyToLocal`    | Copies a sandbox file onto the caller's disk                  |
| `MakeDirectory`  | Creates the directory and any missing parents                  |
| `ListDirectory`  | Lists the entries in one directory                             |
| `Stat`           | Metadata for one path                                          |
| `Remove`         | Deletes a file, or a directory when `recursive` is set         |

A path inside the sandbox is absolute. A relative path, a blank path, or a
path that contains a NUL byte is rejected before the provider call. A local
path for copy may be relative to the caller process. It must be non-blank and
must not contain a NUL byte.

`ReadFile` and `WriteFile` use bytes. Encode and decode text in the caller.
`CopyFromLocal` and `CopyToLocal` use paths on the caller's disk.

`Remove` with an omitted `recursive` flag deletes a file or an empty directory.
Set `recursive` to delete a directory and its contents.

`Stat` on a symlink describes the symlink. Modal can report a symlink. Daytona
reports a file or a directory. `mode` is an octal string when the provider
supplies one, such as `0644`. `size` is a byte count: `int64` in Go and
`bigint` in TypeScript. `modifiedAt` is a timestamp when the provider supplies
one.

An omitted timeout inherits the client deadline. Explicit zero adds no Kit
deadline. Daytona accepts a timeout only as a whole number of seconds. Modal
filesystem methods use the call's context or abort signal as the deadline.

`MakeDirectory` creates missing parents. Modal accepts a directory that already
exists. Daytona returns the provider error when the directory already exists.

```ts
await sandbox.filesystem.makeDirectory("/tmp/kit-files");
await sandbox.filesystem.writeFile(
  "/tmp/kit-files/note.txt",
  new TextEncoder().encode("hello\n"),
);
const data = await sandbox.filesystem.readFile("/tmp/kit-files/note.txt");
const info = await sandbox.filesystem.stat("/tmp/kit-files/note.txt");
await sandbox.filesystem.copyToLocal("/tmp/kit-files/note.txt", "note.txt");
await sandbox.filesystem.remove("/tmp/kit-files", { recursive: true });
console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(data), info.size);
```

}

data, err := files.ReadFile(ctx, "/tmp/kit-files/note.txt", nil)

Creates one Daytona sandbox from the default snapshot, then reads, writes,
copies, lists, and removes files through `Filesystem`. The program deletes the

```sh
cp .env.example .env
```
```sh
# Set MODAL_TOKEN_ID, MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET, and MODAL_APP_NAME
```

# Filesystem

File calls live on the sandbox handle, next to lifecycle. Daytona and Modal
implement the same methods. Open the handle with `Create`, Daytona `Get`, or
Modal `Attach`, then call `Filesystem` / `sandbox.filesystem`.

| You want to                         | Go                | TypeScript       |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------- |
| Read the bytes of one file          | `ReadFile`        | `readFile`       |
| Replace one file                    | `WriteFile`       | `writeFile`      |
| Copy a file from your machine       | `CopyFromLocal`   | `copyFromLocal`  |
| Copy a file onto your machine       | `CopyToLocal`     | `copyToLocal`    |
| Create a directory                  | `MakeDirectory`   | `makeDirectory`  |
| List one directory                  | `ListDirectory`   | `listDirectory`  |
| Read metadata for one path          | `Stat`            | `stat`           |
| Delete a file or directory          | `Remove`          | `remove`         |

Calls on one handle run one at a time, including lifecycle calls. A second
handle for the same sandbox does not wait.

## Paths

A path inside the sandbox is absolute: `/tmp/note.txt`. A relative path, a
blank path, or a path that contains a NUL byte is rejected before the provider
is called. The error field is `path`.

A path on your machine, used by copy, may be relative to the process, such as
`./note.txt`. It must be non-blank and must not contain a NUL byte. A rejected
local path uses the field `local_path`.

## Bytes and disk

`ReadFile` and `WriteFile` move bytes. Encode text before you write it, and
decode text after you read it. `WriteFile` replaces an existing file and
creates missing parent directories.

`CopyFromLocal` and `CopyToLocal` use files on disk. The local file is the
first argument of `CopyFromLocal` and the second argument of `CopyToLocal`.
Copy creates missing parent directories of the destination and replaces a file
that is already there.

## Timeouts

Leave the timeout unset to use the client deadline. Set it to zero when this
call should add no Kit deadline. Daytona accepts a timeout only as a whole
number of seconds, so 1500 milliseconds is rejected and 2 seconds is passed
through. Modal filesystem methods take the context or abort signal as the
deadline.

```ts
const data = await sandbox.filesystem.readFile("/tmp/note.txt", {
  timeout: 2_000,
});
```

```go
data, err := instance.Filesystem().ReadFile(ctx, "/tmp/note.txt", &sandbox.FileReadOptions{
    Timeout: sandbox.Duration(2 * time.Second),
})
```

## Read a file

`ReadFile` returns the bytes of one file. A missing file comes back as not
found. A directory path fails at the provider.

```ts
const data = await sandbox.filesystem.readFile("/tmp/note.txt");
const text = new TextDecoder().decode(data);
```

```go
data, err := instance.Filesystem().ReadFile(ctx, "/tmp/note.txt", nil)
```

[Go Daytona](../examples/go/daytona/read-daytona-file/README.md) ·
[TypeScript Daytona](../examples/typescript/daytona/read-daytona-file/README.md) ·
[Go Modal](../examples/go/modal/read-modal-file/README.md) ·
[TypeScript Modal](../examples/typescript/modal/read-modal-file/README.md).

## Write a file

`WriteFile` replaces the file at that path. Parent directories are created
when they are missing.

```ts
const body = new TextEncoder().encode("hello\n");
await sandbox.filesystem.writeFile("/tmp/kit-files/note.txt", body);
```

```go
err := instance.Filesystem().WriteFile(ctx, "/tmp/kit-files/note.txt", []byte("hello\n"), nil)
```

[Go Daytona](../examples/go/daytona/write-daytona-file/README.md) ·
[TypeScript Daytona](../examples/typescript/daytona/write-daytona-file/README.md) ·
[Go Modal](../examples/go/modal/write-modal-file/README.md) ·
[TypeScript Modal](../examples/typescript/modal/write-modal-file/README.md).

## Copy a file

`CopyFromLocal` reads a file on your machine and writes it in the sandbox.
`CopyToLocal` does the reverse. An existing destination file is replaced.

```ts
await sandbox.filesystem.copyFromLocal("./note.txt", "/tmp/note.txt");
await sandbox.filesystem.copyToLocal("/tmp/note.txt", "./note.txt");
```

```go
files := instance.Filesystem()
err = files.CopyFromLocal(ctx, "note.txt", "/tmp/note.txt", nil)
err = files.CopyToLocal(ctx, "/tmp/note.txt", "note.txt", nil)
```

Into the sandbox:
[Go Daytona](../examples/go/daytona/copy-file-into-daytona/README.md) ·
[TypeScript Daytona](../examples/typescript/daytona/copy-file-into-daytona/README.md) ·
[Go Modal](../examples/go/modal/copy-file-into-modal/README.md) ·
[TypeScript Modal](../examples/typescript/modal/copy-file-into-modal/README.md).

Out of the sandbox:
[Go Daytona](../examples/go/daytona/copy-file-from-daytona/README.md) ·
[TypeScript Daytona](../examples/typescript/daytona/copy-file-from-daytona/README.md) ·
[Go Modal](../examples/go/modal/copy-file-from-modal/README.md) ·
[TypeScript Modal](../examples/typescript/modal/copy-file-from-modal/README.md).

## Create a directory

`MakeDirectory` creates the directory and any missing parents. Modal accepts a
directory that already exists. Daytona returns the provider error when it
already exists.

```ts
await sandbox.filesystem.makeDirectory("/tmp/kit-files");
```

```go
err := instance.Filesystem().MakeDirectory(ctx, "/tmp/kit-files", nil)
```

[Go Daytona](../examples/go/daytona/make-daytona-directory/README.md) ·
[TypeScript Daytona](../examples/typescript/daytona/make-daytona-directory/README.md) ·
[Go Modal](../examples/go/modal/make-modal-directory/README.md) ·
[TypeScript Modal](../examples/typescript/modal/make-modal-directory/README.md).

## List a directory

`ListDirectory` returns the entries in that directory. It does not walk into
subdirectories. A file path fails at the provider.

```ts
const entries = await sandbox.filesystem.listDirectory("/tmp/kit-files");
for (const entry of entries) console.log(entry.name, entry.size);
```

```go
entries, err := instance.Filesystem().ListDirectory(ctx, "/tmp/kit-files", nil)
```

`size` is a byte count: `bigint` in TypeScript and `int64` in Go.

[Go Daytona](../examples/go/daytona/list-daytona-directory/README.md) ·
[TypeScript Daytona](../examples/typescript/daytona/list-daytona-directory/README.md) ·
[Go Modal](../examples/go/modal/list-modal-directory/README.md) ·
[TypeScript Modal](../examples/typescript/modal/list-modal-directory/README.md).

## Read metadata

`Stat` returns one path. A symlink result describes the symlink. Modal can
report a symlink. Daytona reports a file or a directory. `mode` is an octal
string when the provider supplies one, such as `0644`. `modifiedAt` is set
when the provider supplies a time.

```ts
const info = await sandbox.filesystem.stat("/tmp/note.txt");
console.log(info.type, info.size);
```

```go
info, err := instance.Filesystem().Stat(ctx, "/tmp/note.txt", nil)
```

[Go Daytona](../examples/go/daytona/stat-daytona-file/README.md) ·
[TypeScript Daytona](../examples/typescript/daytona/stat-daytona-file/README.md) ·
[Go Modal](../examples/go/modal/stat-modal-file/README.md) ·
[TypeScript Modal](../examples/typescript/modal/stat-modal-file/README.md).

## Delete a file or directory

`Remove` with no `recursive` flag deletes a file or an empty directory. Set
`recursive` to delete a directory and its contents. A directory that still
has entries fails when the flag is omitted. A missing path comes back as not
found.

```ts
await sandbox.filesystem.remove("/tmp/note.txt");
await sandbox.filesystem.remove("/tmp/kit-files", { recursive: true });
```

```go
err = instance.Filesystem().Remove(ctx, "/tmp/note.txt", nil)
err = instance.Filesystem().Remove(ctx, "/tmp/kit-files", &sandbox.RemoveOptions{
    Recursive: sandbox.Value(true),
})
```

[Go Daytona](../examples/go/daytona/remove-daytona-file/README.md) ·
[TypeScript Daytona](../examples/typescript/daytona/remove-daytona-file/README.md) ·
[Go Modal](../examples/go/modal/remove-modal-file/README.md) ·
[TypeScript Modal](../examples/typescript/modal/remove-modal-file/README.md).

| `parents` | Daytona | Modal |
|---|---|---|
| Omitted | Creates missing parents. An existing directory returns the provider error. | Creates missing parents. An existing directory succeeds. |
| `true` | Same as the default. | Same as the default. |
| `false` | Rejected before Daytona is called. The error field is `parents`. | The parent must already exist. An existing directory returns an error. |

```ts
await sandbox.filesystem.makeDirectory("/tmp/kit-files");
```

```go
err := instance.Filesystem().MakeDirectory(ctx, "/tmp/kit-files", nil)
err = instance.Filesystem().MakeDirectory(ctx, "/tmp/ready/nested", &sandbox.MakeDirectoryOptions{

})
```

The second call is for Modal. Daytona cannot turn parent creation off, so that explicit `false` fails in Kit.
